caption: The black and white drawing depicts the façade of a building with three prominent arched doorways at the base, brick patterns indicated on the lower and upper sections, and a plain central band between them. Above the arches, the structure rises to a decorative, curvilinear gable with a central arched opening flanked by two rectangular columns. To the left, there is a smaller arched window set within a square structure topped by a stepped gable. All the architectural details are rendered in shades of gray to black, using stippling and crosshatching to create texture and shading. Below the illustration, there is a ribbon banner with the text “1771” on the left and “mision san antonio de padua” in lowercase letters, both written in a stylized font. The entire drawing is centered on a plain, off-white background with no other visible objects or design elements.
title: Mision San Antonio de Padua
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
